neighbours.label: position right before 'wait' (had to ___ wait, worth the ___ wait, a months-long ___ wait)
fire: The cake took hours to bake, but it was worth the wait.
We never had to wait more than five minutes for a table.
There is a months-long wait for an appointment with a specialist.
Fans will not have to wait long for the next album.
The new bridge opened in May after a decade-long wait.
Customers had to wait in the cold for the doors to open.
I can't wait to see you again next summer.
Patients face a two-week wait for test results.
quiet: The cake took hours to bake, but it was worth the effort.
We never had to pay more than five dollars for a meal.
There is a months-long debate about the new parking rules.
Fans will not have to travel far for the next concert.
The new bridge opened in May after a decade of planning.
Customers had to leave their bags at the front desk.
I want to see you again next summer.
Patients face a two-week course of antibiotics.

notes: promotes ' wait', ' waiting' strongly; top examples are ' to'/' the'/'-long' right before 'wait'
